- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, suggesting overshoot after spikes.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — forecasts often revert to lower levels than true outcomes suggest.
- Late forecast days (last 5–10) are frequently underestimated, indicating lag or underweighting of recent downward trends.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 15–25), possibly due to overconfidence in recent volatility.
- Forecasts often fail to capture sharp downward corrections after initial spikes, suggesting poor handling of short-term volatility.
- Model underestimates true price drops in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, indicating lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp declines, underestimating the magnitude of true price drops.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, leading to overestimation of future prices even when historical mean is lower.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing true trend direction.
